Will create and add a new HOME App on HOME

Parameters:

  • app_name (str) – the desired name/label of the app

  • app_configs (dict) – the configuration dictionary mathcing JSON string

apps_pb2.App

async create_apps(app_configurations: dict[slice(<class 'str'>, (<class 'str'>, <class 'dict'>), None)], timeout: int | None = 'auto', blocking=True) → dict | None[source]¶

Will wait for a series of apps to get created

Parameters:

  • dict[str (app_configurations) – (str, dict)]: Every app to create by name. - {app_name: (app_type, configuration)}

  • timeout (int | None, optional) – Total time to wait for apps to be created. Defaults to ‘auto’. - If an int is given it will use that as the max timeout for all apps to be created - If ‘auto’ is given HAC will figure out a sensible timeout for you - If None is given then only send the create requests and don’t wait

  • blocking (bool) – Will raise an error/warning if True/False. Defaults to True.

Raises:

TimeoutError – raised when a timeout is given but the timeout is exceeded.

Returns:

Wether or not given apps were succesfully created

Examples

hac.create_apps( {

’app_1’: (‘mv’, {‘pips’:12, …}), ‘app_2’: (‘udx, {‘inputResolution’: ‘1080p’, …}), …

}

)

Return type:

dict

async get_all_apps_info(batch_size=50) → list[App][source]¶

Will get the app info of all home apps from the client It will do this by sending a number of requests to HOME based on batch_size Shouldn’t ever have to use this if you’ve already performed an aenter

This uses apps_home.apps_get to get all the apps_pb2.App messages for each app on HOME

The request itself uses regular expressions to locate target apps, these are:

argTplID: str, argAppID: str, argName: str, argAssociatedDeviceID: str, argLocation: str

Other arguments argLimit: int, argStartAfter: str are used:

argLimit - how many apps to return in the given request argStartAfter - the index given from the search start in the loop

Parameters:

batch_size (int, optional) – This affects the size of each request. In testing the system may struggle if this is around 100. Defaults to 50.

Returns:

A list of all apps_pb2.App, for every app matching the request

Return type:

list[apps_pb2.App]

async start_app(target_app_server: LawoAppServer | str | None, app_name: str, version: str, timeout: int = 'auto', timeout_healthy: int = 'auto') → None[source]¶

Will start an app by its name/label on an app server

Parameters:

  • target_app_server (LawoAppServer | str | None) –

    Can be given an App server to start the app on, you can pass a:

    • GUID

    • DEVICE ID

    • APP SERVER LDF DEVICE

    • NONE or ‘auto’ to use auto start

    If ‘auto’ or NONE is passed, the HOME apps mgmt service will pick a server

  • app_name (str) – the label of the app

  • version (str) – version of HOME Apps to use

  • timeout (int, optional) – seconds to wait for the operation to complete. Defaults to ‘auto’ which uses HAC.LifecycleTimeouts.

async start_apps(app_names: list[str], target_app_server: LawoAppServer | str | None, version: str, timeout_start: int | None = 'auto', timeout_health: int | None = 'auto', blocking: bool = True) → tuple[dict, dict][source]¶

Will wait for a series of apps to start on an App Server

Parameters:

  • app_names (list[str]) – A list of app labels

  • target_app_server (LawoAppServer | str | None) –

    Can be given an App server to start the app on, you can pass a:

    • GUID

    • DEVICE ID

    • APP SERVER LDF DEVICE

    • NONE or ‘auto’ to use auto start

  • version (str) – version of HOME Apps to use

  • timeout_start (int | None, optional) –

    Will wait for all apps to start. Defaults to ‘auto’.

    • If an int is given it will use that as the max timeout for all apps to start

    • If ‘auto’ is given HAC will figure out a sensible timeout for you

    • If None is given then only send the start request and don’t wait

  • timeout_health (int | None, optional) –

    Will wait for all apps to report themselves as healthy. Defaults to ‘auto’.

    • If an int is given it will use that as the max timeout for all apps to be healthy

    • If ‘auto’ is given HAC will will figure out a sensible timeout for you

    • If None is given then don’t wait for any healthy

  • blocking (bool) –

    Will raise either errors or warnings when timeouts are exceeded.

    • True: Will raise an error if any given timeouts fail.

    • False: Will only raise warnings if given timeouts fail.

Raises:

  • TimeoutError – (Error on started check) - raised when timeout_start is given but the timeout is exceeded.

  • TimeoutError – (Error on health check) - raised when timeout_health is given but the timeout is exceeded

Returns:

Wether or not a given apps were succesfully started/healthy

Return type:

tuple[dict, dict]
